The Directors can act on every subject a notice tells about, while every Seat would tell people with no authority. A department's money is acted on by whoever wears its hat now, so its current wearers must hear about it, and a person swapped out of the hat must not keep hearing about money they can no longer act on (docs/design/authority.md, contradiction 11). Who wears a hat is an indexed chain fact, so notices reads indexing's hat-wearers (dependencies.of-notices); the Directors stay the company Safe's owners read now (notices.chain-reads).

### notices.refused-address: A refused address fails at once; an outage or a throttle is retried

- **Question:** The mail call fails three ways: PROVIDER_ERROR, RATE_LIMITED, INVALID_INPUT (the recipient refused). Retry which?
- **Chosen:** Retry PROVIDER_ERROR and RATE_LIMITED; record INVALID_INPUT as `failed` at once (`refuse`).
- **Why:** A provider that refused the address will refuse it a minute later too; retrying only delays a record that says so. The devnet's mail sink answers its fail switch as a provider failure (PROVIDER_ERROR), so `dev mail fail` still shows a notice retrying, as its frozen about says. The error codes are the shared vocabulary's; EMAIL_DELIVERY_FAILED stays dropped (vocabulary.drop-email-delivery-failed).

### notices.round-invitation: An investor invited to a round or SAFE is emailed, at low priority

- **Question:** Equity's design says notices reacts to an investor's `invite`. Old Capxul sent no such email. Send one?
- **Chosen:** Send `round-invitation` on `fundraise-investment.invite`, low priority like equity.
- **Why:** concepts.notices and dependencies.of-notices both name 'a round or SAFE invitation', and the equity designer built the transition for it. An invited investor is often outside the company and has no other way to learn of it. Equity is low priority (CONVENTIONS rule 4), so this workflow is too.

### notices.worlds: Notices introduces no world

- **Question:** Which devnet worlds does notices introduce for its refusals?
- **Chosen:** None: notices has no operation, so no refusal; its workflows are proven from other concepts' worlds.
- **Why:** A world is where a refusal is reached from, and notices has no operation. Its workflows are observed from the worlds the operations that cause them already name (organizations' `org-with-pending-invitation` for a resend, budgets' and payroll's worlds), with `dev mail fail` arming a refusal and `dev mail notices` reading the record.

## organizations (63)

### organizations.acceptance-rewrites: Twenty-one acceptance lines rewritten as outcomes (P1)

- **Question:** Which frozen acceptance lines name a mechanism a black box cannot see, and what replaces them?
- **Chosen:** org create 4 (row); org me 1 (fixture), 2 (copied signers), 4 (stored limit); org retry 1 (no-hash attempt); org show 3 (authority hold, receipt-backed), 4 (proof); org wait 1, 2 (scheduled attention); invite list 1 (cursor); invite decline 1 (configuration), 2 (verified), 4 (dispatch, commands), 5 (scheduled event); org invite list 3 (cursor); org invite cancel 1 (triple, configure command), 2 (signed configuration), 3 (verified), 5 (scheduled event); org invite resend 2 (records), 3 (records failed).
- **Why:** P1 option C: keep every claim a black box can check, and turn each line that names a row, a cursor, a scheduled job, a command or a copy into the outcome it guarded, checked by cli, read, chain, trace or world; each keeps its old line and test citation in `was`. A rewrite must still pass against the old system: each says what the old test observed, without the old mechanism (a cursor becomes `--after`, a scheduled event becomes the traced org_invite_transitioned, a stored delivery outcome becomes the mail sink).

### organizations.agent-cover: An agent rides on its owner's Seat, one per Seat; an uncovered agent takes one

- **Question:** 'Every seat can have one agent account, as well as the company's agent.' Whose Seat covers an agent, and what of an agent nobody seated here owns, or a seated person's second agent?
- **Chosen:** An agent's Party names its owner. A person who holds a Seat here covers one agent of theirs; the Organization covers the one agent it owns. An agent nothing covers (an outsider's, another Organization's, a second of the same person's) takes a seat of its own, like a person, while one is free.
- **Why:** It reads the ruling as ten people, each with an agent, plus the company's: up to 21 members. Refusing uncovered agents would take away what `org member invite @handle --agent` does today (any agent can be offered a Seat), so they count as a person does instead. The owner is read from the agent's Party (parties), which organizations already reads; nothing new is needed from agents, which sits above. A covering Seat is a person's, and a person's Seat never ends, so a covered agent never loses its cover; its own Seat ends when the chain removes it, which frees the cover for another. For Aaron, to confirm the reading: does an agent take one of the ten, or ride beside its person's Seat as here?

### organizations.agent-seats: AgentRemoved ends an agent's Seats, as a chain-event workflow

- **Question:** The concept map says an agent's Seat ends when the chain shows the agent removed. How?
- **Chosen:** A workflow triggered by AgentOwner's AgentRemoved removes every active Seat at the agent's Safe.
- **Why:** Agents depends on organizations, so organizations cannot follow its transitions; the chain event is the fact both concepts agree on, and indexing delivers it (dependencies.of-organizations names AgentRemoved).

### organizations.app-commands: Apps: any member lists; a Director or the FDE adds and removes, from a catalogue

- **Question:** How do `org head app list|add|remove` behave: who may run them, which app names are accepted, and what do adding twice and removing a fundamental app do?
- **Chosen:** `org head app list` for any member. `org head app add|remove` for a Director (the Director hat, read from indexing) or the Organization's own agent acting as itself (the Seat whose use is `organization`, a self-run one), as aaron.frappe-shape and aaron.fde-agent have the FDE add apps in conversation; the hosted FDE never acts as itself but as its asker (aaron.fde-anyone), so it adds one for a Director who asks. An app is one of HEAD_APPS, the deployment's catalogue of published Frappe apps a host can install; any other name, or a fundamental app, is INVALID_INPUT at add. Adding an app already wanted or installed answers it as it stands; a removed one is wanted again. Removing a fundamental app is WRONG_STATE, and one the Organization never had INVALID_INPUT. None of them calls the head: the head connection's process installs what is wanted.
- **Why:** Other apps are added at start-up or in conversation with the FDE, so the FDE must be able to add one, and so must a person: a Director, because a connected head's host is then asked to install it, which is the Organization's choice (docs/design/new-commands.md section 3). The FDE is recognised by its Seat's use, so the guard needs no read of agents, which sits above. A catalogue answers the same before any head exists and lets an eval refuse a name; a self-hosted head's own app is its owner's to install and is the head's (organizations.apps-native-or-head). Adding twice being one want matches `want`, a birth. A fundamental app is in every Organization from its first day, so removing one asks for a state none may be in: WRONG_STATE, as G6 gives a forbidden transition.

### organizations.approval-endings: A setup stalled by its install approval keeps approvals' code for the ending

- **Question:** Approvals asks each opener to map an approval's endings onto the frozen codes (approvals.machine). The setup records a stall reason (approval_declined, approval_expired, approval_displaced, install_refused, install_reverted) and a code. Which code goes with each?
- **Chosen:** declined CANCELLED; expired and displaced WRONG_STATE; reverted TRANSACTION_FAILED; refused the code approvals stored.
- **Why:** `org show` and `org wait` print the setup's failure with a code, and agents and board answer their carriers' endings with the same mapping, so one CLI says the same thing for the same ending. The reason stays, because `org retry` resumes from the step it names. No frozen refusal of the setup operations changes: these are the setup's recorded failure, not a refusal.

### organizations.apps-native-or-head: Fundamental apps live in Capxul; every other Frappe app lives on a head

- **Question:** aaron.frappe-shape: other apps are added at start-up or through the FDE. Capxul holds the fundamental apps' records in their Frappe shapes. Where does an added app (Helpdesk, Stock, Manufacturing) live?
- **Chosen:** On a connected head only: Capxul records it in the Organization's app list as wanted, asks the head's host to install it once a head is connected, and never copies its documents. Its documents may name Capxul's records by Capxul id and ask Capxul for money only through Capxul's commands.
- **Why:** For Aaron. Fork as little as possible: a generic store would make Capxul a second Frappe backend that must run every app's controllers to be right, which is a fork in all but name; a concept per app does not scale past a few. The fundamental apps are native because the rulings say every Organization has them from the start, head or no head. So an Organization with no head can want an app but not use it, and the FDE says so and offers to connect a head. Is that the line Aaron means?

### organizations.bind-invitation-grants: New procedure: the proposer binds an invitation to its grants' transaction

- **Question:** Budgets proposes an invitation's grants to the Board, and organizations cannot follow budgets' or board's transitions (it depends on neither). How does the invitation learn which proposal carries its grants, so it can open, or be cancelled, from the chain?
- **Chosen:** Budgets invokes `organizations.bind-invitation-grants` in the transaction that opens the proposal; the invitation then follows that Safe transaction on chain.
- **Why:** Money fact: the grants (hats with authority over the company's money) and the Safe transaction that carries them are one fact, the rules.procedures case 'a chain write and the proposal that carries it'. Bound in one transaction, the invitation never waits on a proposal that does not carry it, and its process decides everything from chain proof: ExecutionSuccess of the bound hash opens it, the nonce going to another transaction cancels it, and the cancel rpc can tell whether the proposal may still run. Waiting for hats cannot know a new allowance's hat, and letting the proposer drive the phase would write organizations' machine from above, a second writer P4 forbids. The invoking transaction calls two concepts' procedures (board.propose and this one), within sys:tx-width.

### organizations.buy-seats: Decision pack: a company buys seats and its FDE's hosting from a budget

- **Question:** aaron.buy-seats: a company may buy more seats itself, paid in stablecoins from the company Safe; a Capxul operator may still raise the limit; the price is Aaron's to set. What is the command, who may run it, how is it paid, and when does the limit rise?
- **Chosen:** Recommended: exactly the 3 commands of docs/design/new-commands.md (section 5.5), in its one grammar: `org seats show` (organizations', any member, read: the limit, what counts against it, the seats bought and SEAT_PRICE); `org seats buy <n> --from <budget>` (payments', chain-submit: a person whose Safe wears the People hat, the hat that invites and so meets the limit, and whom Budgets.authorised admits on the budget, its department's hat or an ancestor's, as the chain reads it; never an agent); and, for the hosted FDE (aaron.fde-hosted), `org fde pay [<months>] --from <budget>` (payments', chain-submit: a person Budgets.authorised admits on the budget; never an agent). Payments books both buys, because organizations sits below payments: each births one command by `payments.prepare-command`'s rules (route budget, owner the Organization, one item to Capxul's receiving Safe for n seats or months times the price, its source naming the count and, for seats, the buyer, never the Organization), and its settlement invokes an organizations door in the settling transaction with the command's owner as the Organization: `organizations.add-bought-seats` raises the limit, and `organizations.extend-fde-hosting` moves the FDE's paid-through instant on by the months (organizations.fde-hosting); each reversal on a reorg invokes its return door. So what was bought counts exactly when the payment settles and only for the company that paid. The prices are the deployment settings SEAT_PRICE (10 USDC a seat, paid once; a bought seat is kept for good) and FDE_HOSTING_PRICE (20 USDC a month) on the test USDC (aaron.test-prices); a price unset for the budget's token is FEATURE_NOT_AVAILABLE.
- **Why:** A decision pack under rules.new-operations, which Aaron accepted as recommended (sixth batch); the prices are set (aaron.test-prices: a seat 10 USDC once, the hosted FDE 20 USDC a month). `org.seats.buy` and `org.fde.pay` (payments') and `org.seats.show` (organizations', organizations.seats-show) serve aaron.buy-seats, aaron.fde-hosted and aaron.test-prices; organizations books the purchases' two doors and the hosting's two (`organizations.extend-fde-hosting`, `organizations.return-fde-hosting`). Since a People-hat wearer holds no department or team office (ROLE_CONFLICT), a buyer spends from an allowance whose hat their Safe wears now, or one above it: a founder who wears only the People hat first has the Board make them an allowance (organizations.founder-people-hat). The hosting is paid on the same route because it is a second thing an Organization buys from Capxul, from a budget, in a stablecoin, counted when it settles; by the month, in advance (organizations.fde-hosting). Organizations cannot birth the payment: `payments.prepare-command` is a door of a concept above it, and depending on payments would be a cycle; so what was bought follows the payment only through a door payments invokes. Counting it in the settlement's own transaction keeps payments' one settlement path (payments.one-settlement-path) and makes 'counted once the payment settles' exact, across a reorg too. A request from Capxul would put an issuer in every purchase; a budget is the route the door already has. An agent never buys (agents.fde-authority). The Organization counted is the paying command's owner, never a value the source carries, so one company cannot buy for another. A seat subscription needs a lapse that lowers a limit, which nothing designs. This pack's `affects` cannot list payments' records (a decision imports only its concept's dependencies), so payments.seat-purchase and payments.fde-hosting-purchase cite it and list `org.seats.buy` and `org.fde.pay`.

### organizations.command-priorities: The start-up's commands are critical: app list and add; the FDE's are not

- **Question:** The grammar makes every new command normal; the commands pass marks the ones a pilot or a start-up needs critical. Which of organizations' nine?
- **Chosen:** Two: `org head app list` and `org head app add`, since a start-up adds the apps its business needs beyond the fundamental ones, a Director directly or through the FDE. `org fde show` and `org fde ask` are normal, with the head's three, `org head app remove` and `org seats show`.
- **Why:** Aaron's ruling aaron.fde-anyone (8 November 2026, night, question 36, which named this record): 'The FDE is not on the critical path anyway.' So start-up's premise, that `org fde ask` is how a founder's first sitting happens at all, no longer holds, and the FDE's two commands are normal: nothing a pilot or a start-up needs waits on them. A start-up still adds the apps beyond the fundamental ones, so `org head app list|add` stay critical. Critical orders the build's work and the evals a start-up depends on; it changes no budget. projects.critical-commands does the same for a pilot's first engagement.

### organizations.command-worlds: Seven worlds for the new commands: a head's site, a head, a hosted FDE's states

- **Question:** Which worlds do the nine commands' claims and refusals start from?
- **Chosen:** Reuse signed-out, two-founders (an outsider names Acme), org-ready (a Director, no head, no FDE), org-with-member (Sam, a member with no hat; Olga outside) and org-with-pending-invitation. Ask devnet for: org-with-head-site (org-with-member plus a stand-in Frappe site for Acme, hosted as on Frappe Cloud, up and not connected), org-with-head (that site connected by Dana as a Frappe Cloud head, whose host installs a wanted app), org-with-head-site-down (the site's fault switch down), org-with-fde (rebuilt for the hosted FDE of aaron.fde-hosted: its key with the stand-in host, its hosting running in its start-up month), org-with-fde-paused (org-with-fde warped past its paid-through instant, unpaid) and org-with-fde-host-down (org-with-fde with the stand-in host's fault switch down); and org-with-fde-allowance (org-with-fde, funded, with a Board top budget, an allowance under it that Dana wears and the payout ceiling set), from which a hosting payment, and payments' `org fde pay` and `org seats buy`, start.
- **Why:** Each refusal needs a state no catalogued world holds: a site to connect, a live head, a hosted FDE paused or unreachable. Building the head worlds from org-with-member keeps Sam (no Director hat) and Olga (outside) in each, so the authority refusals need no world of their own. The paused world is a warp, so it proves the lapse on the one clock (devnet.warp-barrier). A world is shared by every claim that starts from it, so building each once is cheaper than repeating its steps in each eval.

### organizations.commands: Decision pack: the app, head and hosted FDE commands to add (new capabilities)

- **Question:** Adding Frappe apps, connecting a head and reaching the hosted FDE are new capabilities, not among the 215 (aaron.frappe-shape, aaron.frappe-head, aaron.fde-hosted). Which commands does Capxul add, and who may run them?
- **Chosen:** Recommended: exactly the 8 commands of docs/design/new-commands.md (section 5.4), in its one grammar, each one SDK method under `client.org(orgId)` over one rpc in organizations (`organizations.<area>.<verb>`), a flow where it prompts or waits: `org head app list` (any member, read); `org head app add <app>` and `org head app remove <app>` (a Director, or the Organization's own agent, its FDE; write; a fundamental app is never removed); `org head connect <site-url> --host frappe-cloud|self-hosted` (a Director; vendor: a flow reads the head user's API key, and on Frappe Cloud the team's token, from a prompt or a file, never a flag, previews what is shared, and follows the check to connected or failing), `org head show` (any member, read: status, versions, time zone, issue and the apps as the head runs them; each app's sync position is that app concept's) and `org head disconnect` (a Director, write: a flow previews, then one rpc); and, for the hosted FDE (aaron.fde-hosted), `org fde show` (any member, read: its state on the host, its hats, the day its hosting is paid through and FDE_HOSTING_PRICE) and `org fde ask <message>` (any member, or a guest the management names, by aaron.fde-anyone; vendor: a flow sends the message to the host and prints the FDE's reply when its turn ends; the FDE acts as the asker). Paying for the hosting, `org fde pay`, is organizations.buy-seats', since payments books it as it books `org seats buy`.
- **Why:** A decision pack under rules.new-operations. Aaron accepted its app and head commands as recommended (8 November 2026, sixth batch, question 10 of docs/decisions/open-for-aaron.md); the two FDE commands were added after his answer, under aaron.fde-hosted (docs/design/new-commands.md section 6), and who may ask the FDE is put to him in organizations.fde-commands. All eight are booked as operations beyond the 215, with their claims, refusals and worlds (organizations.app-commands, organizations.head-commands, organizations.fde-commands, organizations.command-worlds). The FDE acts through the same CLI as everyone (aaron.fde-agent), so whatever it may do must be a command; an FDE-only surface would put an unchecked path beside the CLI. Connecting a head hands the Organization's records to an outside system, so it is a Director's step, not the FDE's: the FDE prepares it and a Director runs it. Adding an app is reversible and moves no money, so the FDE may do it; any other member may not, because a connected head's host is then asked to install it (agents.fde-authority follows this). aaron.fde-hosted adds two commands no pack listed: the FDE runs on Capxul's host, not beside the founder's CLI, so the Organization needs `org fde show` to see it and `org fde ask` to talk to it through Capxul's own sign-in. Asking was a Director's until aaron.fde-anyone let any member, or a guest the management names, ask, the FDE acting as the asker (organizations.fde-commands, organizations.fde-for-the-asker). The start-up's two (app list and add) are critical, and the FDE's two are not, since it is not on the critical path (organizations.command-priorities). Buying seats and paying the hosting are organizations.buy-seats', and organizations books that pack's `org seats show` (organizations.seats-show).

### organizations.company-safe-address: `begin` computes the company Safe's address in-process

- **Question:** The Party registered at birth needs the company Safe's address before the Safe exists. How does `begin` get it?
- **Chosen:** Compute the minter's pure `companySafeAddressFor` in-process (CREATE2 from fixed inputs), so `begin` stays one write with no node call.
- **Why:** The function is pure, so the backend's computation is checked once against the contract (an eval on the devnet) and never needs a node; a node call would put `begin` in chain-read and make a write fail when a node is down.

### organizations.company-shape: The Organization is ERPNext's Company: abbr, currency, time zone, fiscal year

- **Question:** ERPNext's setup wizard asks for a company's country, currency, time zone, abbreviation and fiscal year. Where do they live in Capxul?
- **Chosen:** On the Organization's row: `abbr` from the name's initials (1 to 5 letters or digits), `default_currency` the country's (Frappe's country_info), `time_zone` the country's first, `fiscal_year_start` ERPNext's for the country or `01-01`; the founder may give any of them at `org create`.
- **Why:** They are the Company's identity for every app, not accounting's alone: projects dates its tasks in the time zone and prices its rates in the currency, payroll's periods follow the fiscal year, and a head's System Settings carries the same zone. In books they would be out of reach of projects and the CRM, which sit below books. It also answers the vision's check C18: whose day a report cuts at is the Organization's time zone. The currency must be one Capxul can value (USD, or one whose USD price pair the deployment lists), because the books value every voucher in it (books.company-settings); a country whose currency has none starts in USD rather than with books that cannot post. Changing one later is not in this design: a time zone or fiscal year that moves under existing books is the books designer's question.

### organizations.create-budget: `org create` takes chain-submit at 4 s / 8 s, not the 2 s / 4 s default

- **Question:** Which budget does `org create` take end to end, excluding the founder's wait and chain confirmations?
- **Chosen:** chain-submit at p50 4,000 ms and p95 8,000 ms.
- **Why:** Before the founder can sign, two service-key transactions are prepared and sent in series (the mint, then deployMoney, which needs the minted Safe) at about 1.5 s p95 each, and the install approval is sponsored (about 1.2 s p95), on top of the begin write. Confirmations are excluded, the sends are not: three hops of the chain-submit class cannot fit its one-hop default.

### organizations.create-refusals: `org create` refusals: FEATURE_NOT_AVAILABLE for the waitlist; no GS026

- **Question:** The frozen refusals of `org create` name no code for a founder still on the waitlist, and the designed text adds ROLE_PERMISSION_DENIED for a batch approved by the wrong Safe. What does the target refuse with?
- **Chosen:** FEATURE_NOT_AVAILABLE for the waitlist (the old code's), WRONG_STATE for an unclaimed Safe (the frozen text), and no GS026 path.
- **Why:** P10: where the book is silent, the old code's behaviour stands, and the old begin refused the waitlist with FEATURE_NOT_AVAILABLE (requireBetaAccess). An unclaimed Safe is the frozen WRONG_STATE, not SMART_ACCOUNT_MISSING. The install approval is only ever opened for the founder's own Safe, which owns the company Safe, so no other Safe can approve the batch and the designed GS026 refusal has no world.

### organizations.declined-previews: Five organizations commands end CANCELLED on a declined terminal preview

- **Question:** Under vocabulary.declined-preview-cancelled a 'no' at a terminal preview ends CANCELLED (exit 130). Which organizations commands ask, and where is CANCELLED listed?
- **Chosen:** `org create`, `org retry`, `invite decline`, `org invite cancel` and `org invite resend` ask at a terminal before they call their one SDK method (their frozen notes: a script must pass `--confirm`; org create 'shows a preview and asks first'). CANCELLED goes in each operation's `errors`, with the CLI's own codes, as `contact add` does.
- **Why:** The CLI asks before it calls the method (org create's flow says so), and three of the five are one rpc with no flow; giving them a flow only to ask would break A4's one-call operation is its rpc. A 'no' writes nothing, and a script passes `--confirm` and never sees the question, so no frozen refusal or exit of a script changes.

### organizations.deployment-row: The deployment is one row written once from the indexed MoneyDeployed

- **Question:** MoneyDeployed is a chain fact indexing already holds. Does organizations keep its own deployment row?
- **Chosen:** Write one row per Organization from the event at finality; it names which hat is which, and never changes.
- **Why:** The concept map gives organizations the deployment ('which officer hat is which') so every concept above can name hats without knowing the install's officer order. The event is emitted once per company and its ids never change, so the row cannot drift, which is what P3's 'nothing copies chain rows' guards against. The install batch is built from it, so the setup needs it anyway. Who wears a hat now, the budgets and the Board's signers stay indexing's views.

### organizations.doc-authority: A family call runs on the head as the member's own User; the head decides

- **Question:** The ruling: 'the caller's authority mapped (a member's hats to the head's roles; a head user matched by mailbox)'. As whom does a family call run on the head, and whose rules decide it?
- **Chosen:** Capxul's backend calls the Capxul app with the connection's key, the member's mailbox and member id, and the roles the member's hats give at that moment (indexing's wearers, read at the call, mapped as organizations.head-users maps them); the app finds the enabled User carrying that `capxul_id` at that mailbox (pushed by organizations.head-users), first brings that User's Capxul-held roles to that set where they differ, as the next push would, and runs the call as that User (`frappe.set_user`), so Frappe's own role permissions, user permissions, permission query conditions, field levels and validations decide, as in its desk. A missing or disabled User is ROLE_PERMISSION_DENIED. Only a person member has a User: an agent's own call is refused, and the hosted FDE acts as its asker's User (organizations.fde-for-the-asker). A guest has no Seat and is refused.
- **Why:** These documents are the head's (organizations.head-ownership: every other app's documents are the head's), so the head's own rules are the authority over them, and running as the member's User applies exactly those rules with nothing copied into Capxul. The roles that User holds are the hats' (People gives HR Manager, which Frappe HR's recruitment, training and onboarding DocTypes grant nearly everything; an Appraisal's cancel and amend are HR User's alone, and a Workflow's actions only its transitions' roles, which Frappe never inherits from another), plus any the head's administrator gave it, which the head trusts for its own documents; they still never authorise a pulled edit of Capxul's records. The hats' roles are set at each call because authority follows the hat at that moment (docs/design/authority.md: a person swapped out loses it), and the push alone runs up to a day behind a hat, which a pulled edit survives (Capxul judges it again) but a family call would not (the head alone decides it). Running as the connection's user would give every member the connection's rights, and a Capxul map of every DocType of every app to a hat would be a second permission model that drifts from the head's. Matching by mailbox and member id keeps a head administrator's User of the same email from standing in for a member. Agents have no User because Frappe keys a User by email (organizations.head-users); an agent works through native commands.

### organizations.doc-family: Decision pack: the document family that reaches what lives only on the head

- **Question:** aaron.sdk-reaches-everything: the Core SDK and the CLI reach every capability, and what lives only on a connected head is reached 'through a generic document family over the SDK (`org doc list|get|create|change|submit|cancel <DocType>`), with the caller's authority, logged, on the world clock' (spelt `org head doc` since organizations.head-group). Which commands, and what does Frappe's own REST API need that those six lack?
- **Chosen:** Recommended: twelve commands in the one grammar (docs/design/new-commands.md section 5.7), each one SDK method under `client.org(orgId)` over one rpc in organizations (`organizations.docs.*`, `organizations.doctypes.*`, `organizations.doc-calls.list`): the six ruled, `org head doc list|get|create|change|submit|cancel <DocType>`; three Frappe's documents need, `org head doc amend` (a cancelled document's correction), `org head doc apply <action>` (a Workflow's step, since a DocType under a Workflow moves only by its actions) and `org head doc remove` (Frappe's Delete, for a draft or a document that is never submitted: a flow that previews); two that say what can be reached, `org head doctype list|get` (Frappe's meta: fields, child tables, Workflow, the member's rights, and why a DocType is not reached); and `org head doc-call list`, the log. Left out: a count (a list pages), copy (create and amend cover it), bulk writes (each document is its own authorised, logged call), whitelisted methods (they write any DocType, a native or a money one, around the family's guard; a head capability that needs one is designed as its own command), and files and comments (Frappe's core module is native).
- **Why:** A pack under rules.new-operations, serving aaron.sdk-reaches-everything; For Aaron: the twelve stand until he answers. The six alone cannot finish what Frappe starts: a cancelled document is corrected only by Amend, a DocType with an active Workflow moves through its actions, whose transitions carry the roles, conditions and self-approval rule the head's approvals are made of, and a draft made in error can only be deleted, since Frappe cancels only what was submitted. Frappe's desk offers a Workflow's document only its actions, but its server does not refuse a direct submit or cancel: validate_workflow checks only a changed state, and set_workflow_state_on_action then sets the state the Workflow gives that docstatus, so the Capxul app refuses `org head doc submit` and `cancel` under an active Workflow itself, as the desk does, and `apply` is the only way through. An agent or a program using the SDK must also learn what a DocType takes before it writes, which is Frappe's meta. A REST proxy would hand the head's whole API, its methods included, to every caller around the guards the ruling asks for. Every family command is `vendor` (G8: it calls the head before it answers), `normal` priority (no pilot and no start-up runs one), area `organizations`, implemented by its rpc except `org head doc remove`, a flow because it previews (G5). The React SDK does not mirror the family: it is the Core SDK's and the CLI's (the ruling draws the line there). The head's two methods, `docRead` and `docWrite`, are the `frappe-head` integration's (shared/external.ts) and the Capxul app's to serve (component frappe-app).

### organizations.doc-log: Every family call is logged once, by its call id, on the world's clock

- **Question:** The ruling says the family is 'logged'. What is logged, when, who reads it, and how does a retry stay one call?
- **Chosen:** `org-doc-calls`: one row per call, read or write, done or refused, written in one transaction after the head answers or Capxul refuses: whose authority (the member, or the FDE's asker with the ask), the head User, the verb, the DocType and name, the outcome and code, field and filter names but never values, the count, the head's `modified` and docstatus after a write, and `at`, the world's now. The SDK method makes the call id once and repeats it on a retry: a logged id answers as logged, and the Capxul app answers a write it already applied under that id as the first time. A call the head did not answer (PROVIDER_ERROR, RATE_LIMITED) is logged refused but is the one row that may change, once: a retry under its id calls the head again, and the row records what the head then answers, with `completed_at`. `org head doc-call list`: a Director reads every call, any other member their own.
- **Why:** Reads are logged too because the hosted FDE now reads for anyone (aaron.fde-anyone), and an Organization must be able to see what was read from its HR records and for whom; Frappe's Version records changes, not reads, and lives on a head that may be disconnected. Names but never values keep Capxul from copying the head's documents (organizations.head-ownership). One call id per invocation makes a create after a lost answer one document, which Frappe's insert alone is not. Logging after the answer, as the FDE's ask does, keeps each rpc to one transaction; a crash between the head's write and the log leaves the write unlogged until the SDK's retry, which the app answers from its record of the call id. A lost answer is the same case seen from the other side: the head may have applied the write, so a PROVIDER_ERROR row that answered every retry as logged would record a write as refused for good and leave the SDK's retry unable to learn the document it made; completing that one row keeps the log true and the write once. A Director governs, so reads every call; anyone else sees what was done with their own authority. `at` is the world's now (aaron.world-clock), and the head stamps its own documents with its now, which follows the same clock (organizations.head-clock).

### organizations.doc-reach: The family never reaches a native DocType, money, or the head's machinery

- **Question:** The ruling refuses the family 'for any DocType a native concept owns (those have their own commands) and for money (Capxul is the system of record)'. Which DocTypes are those, and who decides, Capxul or the head?
- **Chosen:** Four refusals, all INVALID_INPUT with the reason. Native: every DocType of a native app's modules (`org-apps`' `modules`: Frappe's core, ERPNext's accounts and projects, Frappe HR's payroll, Frappe CRM's FCRM), naming that module's commands (NATIVE_MODULE_COMMANDS), and each DocType a native concept holds elsewhere (NATIVE_DOCTYPES: Company, Department, Employee, Customer, Supplier, Contact, Address, Currency, payroll.hr-scope's native HR DocTypes and HR Settings, the WhatsApp app's WA Account and WA Message, and the CRM's email, Communication), naming the commands that reach it. Money: any DocType the head's installed apps list in LEDGER_HOOKS (`accounting_dimension_doctypes`, `period_closing_doctypes`, the advance-payment, bank-reconciliation, audit-trail and repost-allowed lists, merged as frappe.get_hooks merges them) and their child tables; the DocTypes that post or re-post the ledger though no hook lists them (LEDGER_UNHOOKED: ERPNext's Repost Item Valuation); and every DocType of a money module (MONEY_MODULES: Frappe Lending's Loan Management). Machinery: HEAD_MACHINERY, what changes who may do what on the head or what a DocType is, runs code there, moves data in bulk, lets someone with no User write, holds sign-in or outside credentials, or sends through the head's own channels. Child tables: reached only through their parent. Capxul refuses the named lists before any call; the Capxul app refuses by module and hooks, which only the head knows.
- **Why:** Native is a fact of Capxul's book, so Capxul's own list says it, before the head is called; a module's DocTypes change with each Frappe release, so the app reads them from the head's meta. Money cannot be listed once: an app installed later brings its own, and the apps declare most of what posts in these hooks (ERPNext's Stock Entry, Delivery Note, Purchase Receipt, Landed Cost Voucher and Asset; the Sales and Purchase Orders that take advances; Frappe HR's Expense Claim, Payroll Entry, Leave Encashment and Gratuity), so the rule follows the apps. Not all, as reading every posting controller showed: ERPNext's Repost Item Valuation, which the Books hat's Accounts Manager may submit, rewrites past vouchers' ledger entries, and Frappe Lending (in HEAD_APPS) posts from Loan Accrual Repost, Loan Repayment Repost, Loan Transfer and Process Loan Accounting, listed in none of its hooks; so Capxul names the first, takes Loan Management as money whole, and a lane that finds another adds it. An allowlist fails 'everything' the day a customer installs Helpdesk. The machinery is refused because identity is Capxul's (organizations.head-ownership) and each item reaches native or money records, or the world's channels (aaron.world-clock), around the guard: a Custom Field, Property Setter or Workflow changes how a native DocType behaves, a Notification sends and sets fields on any document, a Web Form lets someone with no User write, and the rest run code, move data in bulk or hold sign-in and credentials; Frappe's core module (Server Script, User, Role, Data Import) is native anyway. For Aaron: stock, selling and buying documents post to the ledger, so they are money here and are worked in the head's own desk (books copies their vouchers, books.head-vouchers); drafts-of-money would let the SDK prepare them. NATIVE_DOCTYPES' HR rows are payroll.hr-scope's, and its WhatsApp rows the real app's WA Account and WA Message.

### organizations.doc-worlds: Worlds for the family and for anyone asking the FDE: head documents, guests

- **Question:** Which worlds do the document family's and the FDE commands' claims and refusals start from?
- **Chosen:** Reuse signed-out, org-with-member (no head), org-with-head, org-with-fde, org-with-fde-paused, org-with-fde-host-down and org-with-fde-allowance. Ask devnet for five: org-with-head-docs (org-with-head plus, on the stand-in head, a Designation Accountant; Job Openings HR-OPN-2026-0001 and -0002, both Open, -0002 made a second after -0001 so their `modified` differ; Training Events `Onboarding week` (draft), `Safety training` (submitted, with an employee row) and `Old induction` (cancelled); a Job Applicant named, as Frappe HR names one, by its email, kim@applicants.test, under a Workflow `Applicant Review`, Open to Shortlisted (Shortlist) or Rejected (Reject), Shortlisted to Accepted (Accept), its transitions allowed to HR Manager, the role the People hat gives Dana's User (organizations.head-users), not HR User, which no hat gives; Sam's User with no HR role; the meta's modules, Project in ERPNext's projects; ERPNext's ledger hooks naming Stock Entry), org-with-head-down (org-with-head with the stand-in head's fault switch down), org-with-fde-member (org-with-fde plus Sam's Seat with no hat and Olga ready outside) and org-with-fde-guest (org-with-fde-member with Olga named a guest by Dana, note `Our accountant`), and org-with-fde-head-docs (org-with-fde-member with the stand-in head connected by Dana and holding org-with-head-docs' documents).
- **Why:** Each refusal needs a state no catalogued world holds: head documents in each docstatus and a Workflow, a head that stops answering after it connected, an FDE with a member who wears no hat, and a named guest. The stand-in head must then answer `docRead` and `docWrite` for its documents: Frappe's docstatus rules (submit a draft, cancel a submitted one, amend a cancelled one, never delete a submitted one), the fixture DocTypes' role permissions, their mandatory fields, the Workflow's transitions, the ledger hooks, and a call id it already applied. A real bench (devnet.head-stand-in's escape hatch) stays for a claim that needs Frappe's own validations; none of these does. Two facts of the real systems shape the claims. The stand-in host ends a turn as it is posted, and an ask closes once its turn is read ended, which `org fde ask` does before it returns; so a claim that runs the FDE's commands under an ask holds turns first (`capxul-devnet fault fde-host hold`) and asks with `--timeout-seconds 1`, whose CLI_DEADLINE answer gives the ask's id and leaves it open, then runs them with `capxul-devnet fde run <org> --ask <askId> --`, which devnet adds to its stand-in host. And the head stamps `modified` with the world's now, so on a frozen clock two writes at one instant share a stamp and Frappe's timestamp check cannot tell them apart: the `--modified` claim warps between the two writes. For the devnet designer: these worlds, the stand-in head's family methods and its `drop-answer` fault (the first answer held back once, after the write), and `fde run --ask`.

### organizations.dropped: Old rpcs and workflows that are not ported

- **Question:** The old workspace areas had 46 rpcs and 4 workflows. Which survive?
- **Chosen:** Only what a frozen operation, a flow, a signal or a trigger reaches (P2), and no plumbing (P3): 13 rpcs and 3 workflows, with the grants, officer hats and treasury in their own concepts.
- **Why:** Setups: prepare and submit authorization, the proof receipt and list-mine go to approvals or into `org list`; the ten load, record, accept, fence, claim, apply, recover and emit rpcs are steps of the setup process or the runtime's outbox. Invitations: preview is the budgets flow's read before it writes, get and retry have no frozen caller (a retry has nothing to retry once grants are hats), sweep and expire are each invitation's timer, and the five emit rpcs are transitions' events. Members: grant, revoke, permission-target and record-permission-change are board's officer hats; advance and the legacy states are gone; the emit and notify rpcs are events and notices. Roles: the list is dropped (responsibilities.roles). Treasuries: activity's.

### organizations.event-names: Machines org-setup, org-member, org-invite; org_invite_transitioned stays

- **Question:** What are the three machines called, and so their events (P7)?
- **Chosen:** org-setup, org-member and org-invite, so the invitation's event stays `org_invite_transitioned`, the name the frozen notes use.
- **Why:** The frozen notes of `org member invite` name `org_invite_transitioned`, so a journey or a reader of those notes finds the same event; the prefix also keeps the ids clear of accounts' personal Safe setup and banking's verification invitations. The three old setup events (organization_creation_started, _ready, _failed) fold into org_setup_transitioned. Transition names are verbs (send, accept, decline), so the event's `transition` carries `send` where the old note said `sent`; the new values are listed on the machine.

### organizations.fde-at-start-up: Start-up asks Capxul's FDE host for the FDE; the install batch creates it

- **Question:** aaron.fde-agent: every Organization has a Forward Deployed Engineer, its own agent (aaron.seats). aaron.fde-hosted: it is not on the founder's machine but a durable agent on a durable runtime with sandboxes, which Capxul hosts and the Organization pays for. How is it born at start-up, and where is its key?
- **Chosen:** Unless the founder passes `--no-fde`, the setup's process, once the company Safe is the founder's, asks Capxul's FDE host (organizations.fde-host) to provision the Organization's FDE: the host makes its key, keeps it with the agent's runtime and answers only its address, as the backend sees only an address for every agent. In one transaction the setup records it, computes the FDE's Safe, registers its Party pending and births its hosting (`org-fdes`). The install batch adds `AgentOwner.create(that key, the company Safe)`, so the founder's one signature installs the company and creates the FDE; completion seats it as the Organization's own agent, and the hosting's process starts it on the host. Nothing is made or kept on the founder's machine.
- **Why:** Superseded by aaron.fde-hosted, which answered this record's question to Aaron (where the FDE runs): Capxul hosts it, so its key is the host's, never the founder's machine's. The install batch still carries the create: before the install the founder's Safe is the company Safe's only owner, so the batch calls AgentOwner.create from the company Safe (AgentOwner requires the owner to call) with no Board proposal holding the company Safe's next nonce until the founder answered. Asking the host after the mint, not at `begin`, keeps `begin` one transaction with no outside call and asks only for an Organization whose company Safe is the founder's; the provision is keyed by the Organization's id, so a retried step answers the same key, and a host outage past its retries stalls the setup like any provider (`org retry` asks again). Authority is unchanged (docs/design/authority.md): the company Safe owns the FDE, it starts with no hat (agents.fde-authority) and is never a Director, and hosted it acts only as each turn's asker (organizations.fde-for-the-asker); it is a runtime Capxul operates, and the Board can freeze, re-key or remove it at any time. `--no-fde` stays: hosting is paid (organizations.fde-hosting), so a founder may decline it, and the eval worlds need Organizations without one (organizations.startup-worlds). An Organization started without one gets no hosted FDE later, since no pack lists a command for it; `agent create --org` still makes a self-run agent of its own, with its key on its creator's machine and no hosting to pay (agents.fde).

### organizations.fde-commands: FDE: any member or named guest asks it, and it acts as the asker

- **Question:** The FDE runs on Capxul's host, not beside the founder's CLI. How does the Organization see it and talk to it, and who may?
- **Chosen:** Any member asks, or anyone the Organization's management works with, as a guest it names (`org fde guest add|remove|list`); the host passes the asker's Seat, so the FDE does for them only what their own hats allow (organizations.fde-for-the-asker). `org fde show` as before; `org fde ask` as show-and-ask's flow, for any member or guest; `org fde turn get <turn>` reads a turn its asker stopped waiting for.
- **Why:** Aaron's ruling aaron.fde-anyone (8 November 2026, night; docs/decisions/open-for-aaron.md question 36): 'I think anyone should be able to talk to the FDE, or anyone that the management is speaking to. The FDE is not on the critical path anyway.' It supersedes show-and-ask, the Director-only booking, whose reason was that the FDE acted with the hats the Board granted its own Safe, so whoever instructed it borrowed them; the ruling removes that reason, because the host passes the asker's Seat and the FDE acts as the asker (organizations.fde-for-the-asker): a member borrows nothing, and a write that needs a signature is the asker's own to sign. Who the management works with is a list it keeps, since Capxul cannot know it otherwise (organizations.fde-guests). A surface on the host alone would still put an unchecked path beside the CLI, through which the FDE must act. Recording who asked, but not what, gives the Organization its audit beside each traced command without copying the host's conversation into Capxul. A turn's reply may hold what only its asker may see, so only its asker reads it. The turn is a wait, never system time, so the command's budget is its two host calls.

### organizations.fde-for-the-asker: The hosted FDE acts as its asker: their Seat and hats, their signature

- **Question:** aaron.fde-anyone: 'the host passes the asker's Seat, so the FDE does for them only what their own hats allow'. The FDE signs in with its own key and its Safe wears its own hats. How does a call it makes for an asker carry the asker's authority, and what signs?
- **Chosen:** Each ask mints a fresh act-for token; Capxul keeps its hash on the ask (`org-fde-asks`) and the host gives the token to the FDE's CLI for that turn only (on swarmD, added as a header on the way out, never inside the sandbox). A call the FDE makes with it is the asker's: the tenant guard every concept runs first (organizations' Seat lookup) answers the asker's Seat, Safe and hats in place of the FDE's, while the ask is open: its asker still a member (or an active guest), its turn not read ended, and the world's now before `expires_at` (FDE_ASK_HOURS). Otherwise, or with no token, the FDE's call is ROLE_PERMISSION_DENIED: the hosted FDE never acts as itself. A write that needs a signature opens its approval for the asker's own Safe, and the FDE's SDK, holding no key of the asker's, hands it over (the `--no-wait` answer, or `--json`'s for the payment family) for the asker to sign on the approval page. A command that previews and asks (G5) is the asker's own to answer, so its rpc refuses an act-for call (ROLE_PERMISSION_DENIED). Every span carries the FDE as actor and the asker; records are written as the asker's.
- **Why:** The ruling's words: the host passes the asker's Seat, and the FDE does only what the asker's hats allow. Acting as the asker is exactly that, with nothing for any concept's guard to learn, because the Seat lookup every guard already runs is organizations' and answers the asker. The chain enforces it too: what moves money is signed by the asker's own Safe, so the FDE's key can never spend a hat the asker lacks, which was the objection to letting any member ask (the FDE's Safe holds its own hats, whoever asks). Intersection would make the FDE useless until the Board grants it every hat any asker might use, and then needs every guard rewritten to check two Seats. A short-lived token per ask, hashed in Capxul and held by the host only for the turn, limits what a leaked token could do to one asker for hours on the world's clock, and removal of a guest or the end of a Seat ends it at once. So the hosted FDE needs no hat of its own (agents.fde-authority). For Aaron, to confirm the reading: the FDE then never acts with hats the Board granted its Safe, and every signature is the asker's. For the shared designer: the tenant layer's resolution of an act-for token belongs in the shared rules, and the Core SDK's signing steps hand over under an act-for session.

### organizations.fde-guests: Guests: People or a Director names the outside people who may talk to the FDE

- **Question:** aaron.fde-anyone lets 'anyone that the management is speaking to' talk to the FDE. Capxul cannot know who that is. Who says, how is an outside person reached, and what may the FDE do for them?
- **Chosen:** A list the management keeps: `org fde guest add <email|@handle> [--note]`, `org fde guest remove` and `org fde guest list` (organizations' `org-fde-guests`, one row per person, with its machine). People or a Director names a person (never a member, an agent or an Organization), resolved as an invitee is (`parties.resolve-recipient`) and admitted to the beta in the same transaction (`accounts.admit`, via fde-guest) so they can sign in; notices tells them how to ask. A guest asks with `org fde ask --org <handle>`; holding no Seat, the FDE acting for them reaches only what their own Party is admitted to. Removing a guest ends their asks at once. `org fde turn get` lets any asker read a turn later.
- **Why:** The ruling names two groups: any member, and anyone the management is speaking to. The second is the management's to say, so it names them; inferring it from records would let anyone who was once paid run the Organization's hosted agent, which it pays for. Management is People or a Director: the People hat already decides who comes into the Organization (invitations, Seats), and Directors govern. A guest is a person because a turn is a conversation with someone who signs in, and an agent or Organization has its own way in. Admitting a guest to the beta in the naming transaction is the invitation's own reason (procedures.accounts-admit): a named guest who could not sign in would be named for nothing. The FDE does for a guest only what the guest may do, because the ruling says 'only what their own hats allow' and a guest wears none here; a guest's own dealings with the Organization are already theirs to read through the admissions (rules.counterparty-reads). Reading a turn later closes a gap the ask's deadline left: until now a reply after the deadline could not be read at all. For the accounts and shared designers: `accounts.admit` gains `via` fde-guest; for notices, a guest-named email.

### organizations.fde-handle: The FDE's handle is `<handle>-fde`, or `fde-` and the Organization's id

- **Question:** Every agent's Party has a handle (3 to 30 characters). What is the FDE's, and what if it is taken?
- **Chosen:** `<handle>-fde`, from the Organization handle's first 26 characters; when that is taken, `fde-` and the last ten characters of the Organization's id (`org_<ulid>`), lowercased. Display name `<name> FDE`.
- **Why:** `org create` must never be refused because of the FDE's name, and a founder should not have to choose one. The derived handle is free in practice; the fallback is unique by the id. Its last ten characters are the ULID's random part: the first ten are its instant, which two Organizations born at one frozen instant share (time.read-once), so a fallback cut from them could collide and refuse the second `org create`. Parties keeps both forms for the Organization they name (parties.fde-handles), so nobody else can take an FDE's handle.

### organizations.fde-host: Capxul's FDE host is swarmD: a component and the `fde-host` integration

- **Question:** The FDE is a durable agent on a durable runtime with sandboxes, which Capxul runs for each Organization. What is that runtime in the book, and how does the backend reach it?
- **Chosen:** For aaron.fde-hosted: a component `fde-host`, Capxul's own swarmD namespace on Cloudflare (durable agents on pi-durable, each worker with its own sandbox): one persistent worker per Organization's FDE, keyed `fde:<orgId>`, whose instructions are Capxul's FDE persona and Frappe skills and whose tool is the Capxul CLI signed in with the FDE's key (aaron.machine-login). The backend reaches it through an integration `fde-host` (Effect service `FdeHost`) with calls `provision` (make the agent and its key, keep the key in the host's secret store, answer the key's address), `start`, `pause`, `resume`, `retire`, `send` (post a message with its asker; answer the turn) and `turn` (a turn's state and reply), each idempotent by the agent id. Failures map as other vendors': unreachable PROVIDER_ERROR, 429 RATE_LIMITED, an undecodable answer PROVIDER_RESPONSE_INVALID. Config FDE_HOST_URL; secret FDE_HOST_TOKEN. Its devnet fake is a stand-in host (devnet.fde-host-stand-in).
- **Why:** swarmD is what the ruling describes: a durable agent whose conversation survives restarts in a Durable Object, a sandbox per worker restored from a snapshot, secrets added on the way out so they never enter the sandbox, and an SDK, CLI and MCP surface for the backend; Capxul's own build already runs on it (swarm.superset). Booking the host as an integration keeps every outside call named (CONVENTIONS rule 9): the setup's provision, the hosting process's start, pause, resume and retire, and the ask's send and turn. The backend sees only the FDE key's address, as for every agent. The build pass booked integration `fde-host` in shared/external.ts, with swarmD as its outside system and the backend hosting the service (no component of its own, as Bridge has none), FDE_HOST_URL and FDE_HOST_TOKEN in the environments, and wired each call into its record's `calls`.

### organizations.fde-hosting: The FDE is paid a month ahead from a budget; an unpaid month pauses it

- **Question:** The Organization pays Capxul for hosting its FDE, FDE_HOSTING_PRICE a month, a deployment setting. How is it charged each month through `payments.prepare-command`, and what happens when it is not paid?
- **Chosen:** Under aaron.fde-hosted and aaron.test-prices, in advance by the calendar month, from a budget: `org fde pay [<months>] --from <budget>` (payments', organizations.buy-seats) births one command through `payments.prepare-command` (route budget, owner the Organization, one item to Capxul's receiving Safe for the months times FDE_HOSTING_PRICE, its source naming only the months, 1 to 12), signed by a person Budgets.authorised admits on the budget. Its settlement invokes `organizations.extend-fde-hosting`, moving `paid_through` on from the later of `paid_through` and the settlement; a reorg's reversal invokes `organizations.return-fde-hosting`, which takes back exactly the span that payment added (calendar months from a later start do not subtract back). The first month is the start-up's, from the setup's readiness. Each month the hosting falls due seven days before `paid_through`, and notices reminds the Directors with the command to run. Unpaid at `paid_through`, the host pauses the FDE: it takes no turn and its sandbox stops; the host keeps its key, conversation and workspace; nothing on chain changes; `org fde ask` is WRONG_STATE. Paying again wakes it and the host resumes it. A paused FDE is kept until paid or removed by the Board. With no price set, hosting is not charged.
- **Why:** Paying in advance through `payments.prepare-command` is the route seats already take: one settlement path, one book fact, counted only when the payment settles and only for the Organization that paid, and nothing for Capxul to collect. The payment is the department's whose budget pays: whoever wears its hat, or one above it, now (docs/design/authority.md); the FDE never pays for itself, as no agent buys from Capxul (G4). A standing agreement makes Capxul a payee that must collect, and dated payments reserve a budget's room months ahead, which a department would not expect. Pausing, not retiring, keeps what the FDE learnt and changes nothing on chain, so its authority is as before when it resumes; months run from the payment, so a pause is never charged. The start-up month exists because the FDE must set the Organization up before anyone can pay: at the install the company's top budget is 0 and no budget is funded. No price, no charge, so `org fde pay`'s FEATURE_NOT_AVAILABLE means what it says. Payments' booking (payments.fde-hosting-purchase) checks a hosting that is not retired and a price set before the command is born. For Aaron (docs/design/new-commands.md section 7, question 2): paying in advance by the month stands until he answers; the alternative is the standing agreement, an automatic monthly charge.

### organizations.fde-seat: The setup seats the FDE before it signs in; it serves only its Organization

- **Question:** The FDE's Seat is the Organization's own agent's (seat_use organization). When is it born, and can the FDE sit in another Organization?
- **Chosen:** Born with the founder's when the setup completes, `seat_use` organization, its `principal_id` null for good; an agent's session is matched to a Seat by its Safe, by every concept's tenant guard. Another Organization's own agent is never offered a Seat (INVALID_INPUT at invite).
- **Why:** An invitation would need someone to invite the FDE and the FDE to accept before it could help, and the ruling says it is the Organization's from the start. A null principal is what agents already says of an agent's account before its first sign-in (agents.account-at-first-sign-in), and access holds one principal per Safe, so matching an agent by its Safe is the same guard. Nothing writes the Seat when the FDE first signs in (access, below, cannot, and a reaction would leave a window), so an agent's Seat is looked up by Safe, never by principal. The FDE's owner is its Organization's Board, which can freeze, sweep or remove it; seated elsewhere, another company's Board would control an agent working inside this one. Ending an FDE's Seat is the chain's, as for every agent (AgentRemoved).

### organizations.flows: Seven flows, seven single rpcs

- **Question:** Which operations need a Core SDK flow, and which are one rpc call (A4)?
- **Chosen:** Flows: `org create` and `org retry` (rpcs, the approval page, waits), `org show` and `org wait` (find the one unfinished setup when no Organization is given), `use org` (list, then save), `org member get` (the list, then a pick), `invite list` (its own offers, or with `--org` the Organization's). The other seven are one rpc each.
- **Why:** A4: the CLI calls one SDK method, so whatever composes rpcs or saves local state is the SDK's flow. `org show` and `org wait` find 'exactly one unfinished setup' only by listing; `org member get` must 'read the member from the same list'; `invite list --org` lists an Organization's invitations instead. The founder signs the install on the approval page in the browser, so the flows open it and wait, and call no approvals rpc; `org show` and `org wait` share the live setup rpc.

### organizations.founder-people-hat: A founder wears the People hat, so holds no department until it is revoked

- **Question:** The setup mints the People hat to the founder (the founder wears Books, Invoicing and People), and a People-hat wearer may hold no department or team office (ROLE_CONFLICT: budgets.role-conflict-people-hat, board.people-hat-role-conflict). People are swapped in and out of departments by hat. What may a founder do with a department's money, and where is that said?
- **Chosen:** Keep both (aaron.departments), and say the consequence in the founder's journey: while the founder wears the People hat they are never swapped into a department or team. They pay as the Board (while the only Director, a Board proposal needs only their signature) or from an allowance, whose hat sits under the Board's top hat and is no office, and they offer agreements only from an allowance. To run a department themselves, the Board first grants the People hat to another member and revokes the founder's.
- **Why:** The frozen behaviour holds both: org-ready's founder wears the three officer hats, and ROLE_CONFLICT is a frozen refusal, the separation of duties between who manages people and who spends a department's money. On v4 the People hat grants no money authority (offices and allowances are minted by the Board or an office above), so the conflict guards a product rule, not a chain power (docs/design/authority.md). A solo founder is not blocked: as the Board they pay, schedule and create budgets with their one signature, and an allowance gives them a budget of their own to spend from, which is also what `org seats buy` spends (organizations.buy-seats). Exempting the founder would empty the rule for the person it most often meets; minting no People hat would break the frozen worlds and leave nobody able to invite. So the rule stays and is said where a founder meets it.

### organizations.frappe-app-fields: The Capxul app's Custom Fields, one Party field, and what listChanges reports

- **Question:** The four Frappe lanes each asked the Capxul app for Frappe for Custom Fields and changes, under names that differ (the CRM's and the books' `capxul_party`, payroll's `capxul_party_id` on Employee). Which fields does the app add, and what must `listChanges` catch?
- **Chosen:** `capxul_id` and `capxul_version` on every synced DocType. One Party field, `capxul_party`, on Contact, CRM Organization, Customer, Supplier and Employee (payroll's `capxul_party_id` takes this name); a Party in any other role is named by role (`capxul_payee_party` on Salary Component). `capxul_hidden` on Contact and CRM Organization. Each app concept's own fields by its decisions (payroll.head-sync's on Salary Structure Assignment, Payroll Entry and Salary Slip); on User, a member's `capxul_id` and `capxul_party` (organizations.head-users). The app finds or creates a document Capxul names by `capxul_party` (parties.head-parties) and makes the link records it names first (CRM Industry, CRM Lead Source, CRM Territory, Currency). `listChanges` reports every synced DocType (the CRM's Contact, CRM Organization, CRM Lead, CRM Deal; projects', payroll's and the books') and every write path: a document event (`on_change`, which Frappe runs for a save, a submit, a cancel and a `db_set`) appends a change row naming the document, and `frappe.db.set_value`, which runs no event, is caught by `listChanges` itself, which first appends a row for each synced document whose `modified` is later than its own last row recorded. A row names the document; its fields are read as they stand when `listChanges` answers, so a raw write in the same request as a recorded change (Frappe CRM restoring a new deal's `deal_owner` with `update_modified=False`) is reported with it. On a connection's first call it lists every document the site already holds.
- **Why:** The component is one app and one seam, so one name per meaning: two Party fields on Employee would let them disagree, and a lookup by Party must work the same for a voucher's party, a contact and an employee. Reporting every write path matters because Frappe CRM converts a lead with `db_set` and `set_value`, which run no `on_update`, so a hook on saves alone would lose a conversion; reporting what the site already holds on the first call lets a head connected late be adopted (contacts.head-mapping). Renaming a CRM Organization also rewrites the `company_name` of its Contacts, a Data field `rename_doc` does not follow. Every person's Seat is a User whose Contact carries the member's `capxul_party` (organizations.head-users), and a won deal's Customer the head makes (`create_customer_on_status_change`) is the head's, given the `capxul_party` of what Frappe makes it from: the deal's CRM Organization (a Company customer) or, with none, its primary Contact (an Individual), and none when that has no Party. The `modified` sweep is needed because Frappe CRM writes CRM Lead (`update_lead_contact`) and CRM Deal (a Contact's mailbox change) with `frappe.db.set_value`, which no hook sees. Payroll's own field list is payroll's; this records only the shared names.

### organizations.head-claims: Each head command claims what it really does: its answer, its writes, a retry

- **Question:** Five of organizations' commands beyond the 215 carried one acceptance claim each: `org head show`, `org head doc submit`, `org head doc amend`, `org head doctype list` and `org fde guest list`. Which further claims does each behaviour already booked have, observable through the CLI from a catalogued world?
- **Chosen:** Claim what each one's rpc already books, and nothing else. `org head show`: the apps as the head runs them; it reads only Capxul's rows, so it answers while the head is down; failing at the daily check that fails and connected at the next good one (organizations.heads.watch's `stall` and `recover`); `rungAt` on the world's clock (organizations.heads.ring). `org head doc submit`: the head User and the world's clock in its log row; a DocType that is never submitted refused; a retry under the same call id submits once (organizations.doc-log). `org head doc amend`: the amendment is a draft to submit, the original stays cancelled; an amendment's amendment is `-2`; a retry amends once. `org head doctype list`: `--module`, and a native module naming its commands; no child table; paging by name; the call logged. `org fde guest list`: removed guests after active, `--status`, paging, no write.
- **Why:** A claim is an eval, and one claim leaves the rest of a command's booked behaviour untested: what it answers, what it changes and what a retry does. Each added claim restates a sentence of its rpc's or process's about, from a world the catalog holds (org-with-head, org-with-head-down, org-with-head-docs, org-with-fde-guest) and never an invented behaviour. Two were left out as unsure: a submit under an active Workflow (the world's only Workflow runs on Job Applicant, which Frappe HR does not submit, so the refusal it would meet first is not booked), and amending one cancelled document twice (Frappe would name both amendments `-1`). For the devnet designer: the stand-in head's metas need Job Opening not submittable (hrms@8816102: no is_submittable) and Training Event Employee a child table of Training Event (istable), Project in module Projects, and its daily check to fail while its fault switch is down. Truth review, 9 November 2026: two more for devnet. The stand-in names an amendment of an amendment by Frappe's Amend Counter (`Old induction-1` amended is `Old induction-2`, frappe@1a7ea57 naming.py `_set_amended_name`), not `<name>-1` again. The world's Training Events carry hrms' mandatory fields (event_status, type, location, start_time before end_time, introduction: training_event.json, `validate_period`), since the submit and amend claims submit them through the family, which checks them. Here: the per-app versions `org head show` prints are the head connection's process's `check` step's, now booked there. `org head show`'s failing claim reads the stall's issue `at`, which the stall records, rather than `checkedAt`; the amend retry reads the one document amended from `Old induction`.

### organizations.head-clock: A head runs on the one clock: Capxul's times for money, one time zone for days

- **Question:** The one clock (time.one-clock) runs the larger system too. How does a connected head follow it?
- **Chosen:** Money's times are Capxul's (a voucher is dated at its fact's block); a head's own dates are Frappe's, read through frappe.utils; every instant crosses as UTC and every day in the Organization's time zone, which the head must share (else the connection stalls). On a devnet the Capxul app is a follower: it sets now_datetime to the clock's now, runs Frappe's due jobs at each stop, and reports only daily-or-slower jobs as its next due.
- **Why:** ERPNext reads time almost only through Frappe's helpers, and Frappe's tests already freeze them, so following the clock is one patch in the Capxul app, not a fork (docs/vision/erp.md section 5). A head in another zone would put a task's due day or a fiscal year's first day on another date. Reporting only slow jobs as stops follows the barrier's own rule, because Frappe's every-tick and 15-minute jobs would make a simulated year hundreds of thousands of stops; which of Frappe's jobs count as stops is the devnet designer's to fix with the stand-in head.

### organizations.head-commands: Head: a Director connects after a preview; any member reads; no secret in a flag

- **Question:** How do `org head connect|show|disconnect` behave, and where does the site's check happen?
- **Chosen:** `org head connect` (aaron.frappe-head) is a flow: it reads the key and secret, and on Frappe Cloud the team's token and name, from a prompt or files; previews what is shared and asks; connects in one write that seals the secrets and births the connection, whose process checks the site; and follows `organizations.heads.show` live until connected or failing, ending with the issue's code (PROVIDER_ERROR unreachable; WRONG_STATE no Capxul app, another time zone or currency; ROLE_PERMISSION_DENIED a refused key). `org head show` is that read, once, for any member: the connection's own fields and the apps, never a secret, and not each app's sync position. `org head disconnect` is a flow that reads the live head (none is WRONG_STATE), previews and asks, then calls one rpc, keeping every record. Connect and disconnect are a Director's (the Director hat, from indexing), never an agent's.
- **Why:** Connecting hands the Organization's records to an outside system, so a person who governs runs it, a Director (organizations.head-connection); the FDE prepares it and asks. Leaving the check to the connection's process keeps the rpc one transaction and the check in one place, with the same reasons and retries on the first check as on any later one; the flow's live follow gives the person the answer the rpc would have. Secrets in flags end up in shell history and process lists (G5). Each app's sync position is in its own concept's tables, which organizations cannot read (P4): a member reads it through that app's records. Disconnecting keeps Capxul's records, which is what makes connecting safe to try. A preview is a prompt the SDK method asks, and the CLI calls one method (A4), so both head writes that preview are flows, as `contact link` and `org hr employee leave` are.

### organizations.head-connection: A head connection is organizations' record and process; each app syncs itself

- **Question:** The head ruling: connecting a head is a separate step. What records it, and who syncs what?
- **Chosen:** `org-heads` holds the one live connection (site, host, sealed key, what the site said) and its process checks the site and installs wanted apps; each app concept syncs its own records from the connection's `confirm`, through the `frappe-head` integration.
- **Why:** Every app concept depends on organizations, so each can read the connection and follow its transitions; a head concept above them all would have to write every app's tables, which P4 forbids. One live connection at a time keeps one head per Organization's data. The API key is sealed under record-bound encryption bound to the row, as banking seals bank details, and never returned; so are the ring secret (a signature is checked with the secret, not its hash) and, for Frappe Cloud, the team's token its site API needs to install an app, which no site key can. Connecting is a Director's step, because it hands the Organization's records to an outside system (organizations.commands).

### organizations.head-doorbell: The head rings a doorbell with no data; Capxul pulls with its own key

- **Question:** How does Capxul learn that something changed on the head, without polling it every minute?
- **Chosen:** The Capxul app posts a signed, data-free ring after a change commits; it wakes every app's sync, which pulls; a daily pull catches a lost ring.
- **Why:** A minute-scale poll is a timer the one clock would stop at, half a million stops a simulated year (devnet.warp-barrier), and a load on every head. A webhook with data would make the head a writer into Capxul holding Capxul's trust; a ring carries nothing, so a forged one is refused and a replayed one only causes an extra pull, and every change still comes through Capxul's own read with Capxul's own key. On a devnet the stand-in head rings at the stop its scripted edit happens.

### organizations.head-fit: A refusal names the record's group and both sides; the FDE reads as its asker

- **Question:** Fit review of the surface pass (9 November 2026; Aaron: 'It's the logical groupings'). After the rename, the commands the family's refusals name still followed the old nouns' pairing, not the tree's groups: the Payroll module named `org payroll` and `org hr employee`, Projects three of its group's records, and two HR rows only one side. The org-apps index said `org show` lists the installed apps, and `org fde guest list`'s first claim promised the order and the paging its two new claims prove, while its about never named `--status`. And the who of every member read (`org head show`, `org head app list`, `org fde show`, `org fde guest list`, `org seats show`) said 'the FDE included', though the hosted FDE never acts as itself. What should each say?
- **Chosen:** Each pointer names the record's group, with the person's side where one has it, as surface.hr-group places HR. Payroll module: `org payroll` and `payroll`, and `org hr advance settle` for an advance's Additional Salary. Projects module: `org projects`, with its `member`, `settings`, `task`, `timesheet`, `activity-type` and `project-type`. Leave Allocation adds `hr leave balance`; Employee Checkin names `hr attendance checkin` and `list`. `org head doctype list`'s claim names both sides of Leave Application and Expense Claim, as the refusal does. The index names `org head show`. The guest list's first claim says what its evidence shows (the note and who named them), and its about names `--status active|removed` and the paging. A member read's who says the hosted FDE reads only as the member who asked it, and a self-run own agent as itself.
- **Why:** Employee is ERPNext Setup's (erpnext@6b946b0 employee.json: module Setup), not the Payroll module's, and has its own NATIVE_DOCTYPES row naming `org hr employee`. Naming it for the Payroll module sent a Frappe reader asking after Salary Slip or Employee Incentive to HR, and left out the person's side (`payroll payslip`, `payroll agreement`), while every two-sided HR row names both. The one Payroll-module DocType a command outside the payroll group writes is an advance's Additional Salary (payroll.advance-recovery). Projects is one group now, so all of it is under `org projects`, Activity Type and Project Type included. `hr leave balance` reads Leave Allocations, and `hr attendance list` prints your check-ins (payroll's operations). `org show` runs client.org.setup.get, which never reads org-apps; `org head show` and `org head app list` do. A claim's title is what its evidence proves, so the title no longer repeats what claims 2 and 3 prove. docs/design/authority.md: 'A call with no live token is refused, so the hosted FDE never acts as itself', which MEMBER_GUARD already does; only the who said otherwise. Text only: no rpc, guard, refusal code or behaviour changes.

### organizations.head-group: The head's apps, documents, DocTypes and call log are spelt under `org head`

- **Question:** Aaron, 9 November 2026: 'The number was not the issue. We need everything you can do on Frappe to be programmatic and accessible from our tooling. It's the logical groupings.' surface.head-group puts the Frappe site's commands in one group, `org head`. How does organizations apply it to the fifteen commands it booked under `org app`, `org doc`, `org doctype` and `org doc-call`?
